dossier.public_summary: The dip is driven by a few unusually deep transits in a few sectors with no stable depth across all sectors, so it is not a steady planet transit on the target. The centroid cannot confirm the signal is on the target and a nearby star can fully explain the signal, making a blended eclipsing binary the best explanation.

reasons.why: Depth not consistent: chi2 269.74148924651826 dof 13. Share of top 3 = 0.946 and top transits are 1836 ppm (10.8 sigma), 1372 ppm (7.6 sigma), 964 ppm (5.0 sigma) vs mean 396 ppm, a few deep events drive the signal.
Strong sector depth change: depths 484, 748, 59, 52, -41, 521 ppm (chi2 62.23 dof 5). sector_depths_by_source verdict = changes_within_a_source with p_constant 0.0002833750559347306 for SPOC 2-min.
centroid_all verdict inconclusive, why: no sector with a clear difference image, so cannot locate dip on target vs neighbour.
One neighbour within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) could cause the 393.1 ppm dip with an eclipse <=25%, plus several more that need deep eclipses, blended neighbour plausible.
Independent Scorer ranks planet-like at 0.08, far below median planet 0.5, consistent with false positive; similar candidates mostly not a planet (blend).
